rationale: The buyer is concrete and identifiable — IT consultants and sysadmins billing hours for enterprise SSO integrations — and they are already in a paid context (working for clients with Microsoft Entra ID licenses, which start at ~$6/user/month). The problem is highly specific, well-documented by a real practitioner (929-line config file), and an interactive Apache+Entra ID SSO config generator is a near-perfect Claude use case: takes structured inputs and outputs a validated, annotated config file. All four build gates are met (operational_autonomy 8, buildability_with_ai 9, buyer_clarity 8, willingness_to_pay 7), and the service can be delivered fully self-serve. The main gap is zero responsiveness signal — one validation round with 20 outbound messages to sysadmin forums is advised before full launch.
solution_plan: The micro-service is an interactive Apache + Microsoft Entra ID SSO configuration generator: the consultant fills in a short form (tenant ID, redirect URI, Apache version, module), and Claude produces a complete, annotated `mod_auth_openidc` config file with step-by-step instructions — taking a 929-line opaque sample down to a working 50-line config. BUILD: the factory creates a web form with ~8 fields, a Claude prompt that generates the config with inline comments, and a Stripe payment link ($29 one-time per generated config, or $49/mo unlimited). No coding by Youval — factory handles the form, prompt, PDF/text output, and payment. SELL: the factory drafts targeted posts in r/sysadmin, ServerFault answers, and Microsoft Entra ID community forums (linking to the tool as a solution to a common question); each post draft is approved by Youval before publishing. MAINTAIN: user fills the form, pays via Stripe, Claude generates and emails the config file — fully automated. Youval's only recurring involvement is approving outreach drafts and monitoring for edge-case failures (e.g. unexpected Apache versions). This is genuinely viable for a solo non-technical operator.
notes: All build gates met. Responsiveness signal is 0 (untested) — recommend 20 targeted posts/DMs before scaling spend. Frequency is moderate (consultants encounter this once per client engagement, not daily), which caps long-term MRR unless expanded to other SSO providers (Okta, Google Workspace) or other web servers (nginx, Tomcat).
